problems: One state or two: Cliopatria's 'Holy Roman Empire' (962..1259) and 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' (1260..1806) are one empire (Q12548, same article). The brief says to merge rows of one state under the earlier slug, but the eu-08-b dossier holy-roman-empire already exists, ends 1259 and names this dossier as successor, so two linked dossiers were written (one colour, family germany). The orchestrator may merge them; all keyframe ids here start 'holy-roman-empire-minor-states_'.

The row is the Empire's residual, not the whole Empire: great members (Bavaria, Habsburg, Bohemia, Saxony, Brandenburg, Trier, Lorraine, Swiss, Savoy, Milan, Venice) are separate leaf shapes under the umbrella. 81 of 121 events are conf-1 records of Cliopatria leaf cut-outs or returns that no opened page dates.

Nine keyframe corrections: new 1268-1271 Swabia keyframes (Hohenstaufen page), 1415-1421 Mark Brandenburg removed, 1564-1571 about 252 Baltic cells removed (the Livonian Confederation, named 'Livonian Conference' in Cliopatria, was never Imperial), 1629-1631 Mecklenburg kept in the row against the Habsburg Monarchy shape, 1632-1634 Swedish-held cells kept under occupation, 1696/1697-1699 Ryswick return applied in 1697 not 1700, 1806 remnant shortened to the Confederation of the Rhine and the dissolution of 6 August 1806. The Habsburg Monarchy dossier may disagree about 1629.

The WebFetch text of the Holy Roman Empire article stopped at the opening of the Thirty Years' War (88,640 characters on the page), so later passages (Imperial Circles, Pragmatic Sanction, Franche-Comte 1678) could not be cited.
Cliopatria draws 16 Schleswig cells (Syddanmark) inside the row 1662-1712, probably wrong; left as drawn and flagged in the notes.
The Seven Years' War page does not explain the Electorate of Hanover shape taking 81 cells of Hesse and Westphalia in 1757; 1757-1763 moves are treated as page-silent re-cuts.

The page budget of 14 was fully spent; the Palatinate, Wurttemberg, Hesse and the prince-bishoprics are states Cliopatria lacks and are named only through neighbouring shapes in the 1648, 1803 and 1806 events.
